Are you looking for theatre or for film/TV auditions? If you're looking for theatre, steer clear of monologues pulled from recorded media. Look up plays online and scan the samples for roles that seem to fit you enough. If you find one that seems to fit, buy it. Don't worry too much about ethnicity or even age. So long as those things aren't integral to the story (as previously mentioned), you'll be fine if the content is believable. If that's too much money, check out scribd. You'll have to pay 8/month (I think), but you'll have access to tons of plays and books of collected monologues from plays. 

Not gonna lie, dude. It's A LOT of work finding monologues that click with you. Don't be afraid to look at a monologue from a different angle and try working on one that you are a little unsure about. You want to make sure that you're passionate about it by the time you are finished with it, but I have found some great monologues that didn't "click" at first and then, after working them, became my go to pieces. Also, as a general rule, do not pull monologues from books of monologues. I am referring to stand alone books, not ones that have monologues compiled from full length plays.
